title: What If the Arctic Ocean Had No Summer Ice? 2030s Maybe

scenes.text: What if the Arctic Ocean had no summer ice? A study says it could happen in the 2030s.
Scientists call it ice-free below one million square kilometers, in an ocean of about 14 million.
The first ice-free September could come between 2030 and 2050, a decade earlier than expected.
Dark open water soaks up more heat than white ice, so the Arctic warms even faster.
September ice is already shrinking about 12.6 percent per decade, according to NASA.
Researchers link the loss to heatwaves and wildfires farther south. Only the summer minimum would vanish.
